incidents.what: Ran a t31 cold-cache rehearsal that re-tokenized en_c4 single-process while 44 already held a warm cache and had 8 encoders running; my job starved theirs and the run was killed by the 120s startup gate mid-tokenize.
incidents.evidence: runs/t31_rehearsal.log (single 'mix: tokenizing en_c4 (7767463 docs, workers=1)' line, no step lines); facts/efficiency.json#eff.cache_load_gates_startup (contended rate 0.07 GiB/s vs 0.39 effective)
incidents.root_cause: I checked that the cards were idle and treated that as the pod being free, when the contended resource was CPU and page cache, which nvidia-smi does not show.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: launch_30b.sh no longer names a gate at all and harness launch derives it from the mix's cache bytes, so a slow load cannot be mistaken for a hang; proposing a --dry refusal when any domain's cache is cold (fb's option B).
incidents.differently: Before starting anything on a shared host, enumerate what the job actually consumes (cards, CPU, page cache, disk) and check each, and ask the owner of a cache before rebuilding it.

incidents.what: Closed register tasks t01 and t02 by running `harness task done` on the pod. runs/tasks.jsonl in the repo is canonical and the pod copy is push-only, so both closes were silently lost.
incidents.evidence: runs/tasks.jsonl (t01/t02 closed in the repo only after fb's correction); scripts/pod_push.sh (pushes tasks.jsonl to the pod, never reads it back)
incidents.root_cause: I assumed a file present on both sides was synchronised in both directions; the sync is one-way by design and nothing refuses the write on the read-only side.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: proposed: `harness task` should refuse to run when it detects it is on the pod (the same one-line guard shape as its existing worktree check at scripts/harness.py:2491), rather than succeeding into a file nobody reads.
incidents.differently: For any state file that exists on both sides, establish which copy is canonical before writing, not after.

incidents.what: Reported 1.5-1.6 GiB/s to fb as the measured cache-read rate and sized the stage-1 gate from it. That is a single reader on an idle disk; a 7-rank startup shares the page cache and gets 0.39 GiB/s. A gate derived from 1.5 is 192s, under the 600s floor, so it would have looked correct and done nothing. My 1800s was safe by accident, not by derivation.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused, caught by de before it shipped
incidents.evidence: facts/efficiency.json#eff.cache_load_gates_startup (three rates separated: 0.39 per-rank startup, 1.55 single-stream warm, 1.30 raw dd, 0.07 contended); commit ad89736
incidents.root_cause: I measured one regime and reported it as the property, with no note of the regime it was measured in -- single-stream and 7-rank-concurrent differ by 4.0x.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: the fact now names all three rates and which one predicts the gate; harness launch owns the derivation via _CACHE_READ_GIBPS; two docstrings that still said 1.5 GiB/s now point at the constant.
incidents.differently: State the regime beside every rate, and when a number will be used to size something, measure it under the conditions it will be used in.

incidents.what: Wrote a fallback pod-sync script whose delete logic produced catastrophic false positives -- it would have deleted live train.py and harness.py from either a HEAD~1 or a pod-manifest baseline.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused, caught by my own dry run before it ran
incidents.evidence: the script was never committed; superseded by de's scripts/pod_push.sh --all
incidents.root_cause: I inferred 'absent from the baseline' meant 'should be deleted', when it also means 'the baseline is incomplete' -- and the baseline was.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed by deletion: dropped my script entirely once pod_push.sh --all existed.
incidents.differently: A destructive path needs its own dry run against the real tree before it is written, not after; and prefer waiting for a peer's tool over shipping a parallel one.

class_removed: pending: startup-gate kills from a slow load are now derived rather than guessed (landed); next is the cold-cache refusal in launch_30b.sh --dry so a launch cannot begin against a cache that has to be built first.
note: Retro written while pretrain_15b_s1 is running (step 530, loss 2.109, 77K tok/s/GPU, MFU 32%). No code change to the launch path until the run is past step 1000, per fb; the block stays untouched.

incidents.what: eval_hard/code/math.sh set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$i, the shard index. A lane-card launch (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7) of eval/code_zh.py landed shard 0 on physical GPU 0, a training-block card, and blocked tilerl-4c's t01.
incidents.caused_or_missed: missed; caught by tilerl-4c watching nvidia-smi, fixed in 2f97e4a
incidents.evidence: commit 2f97e4a is the only record: no experiments row, no lesson entry, no retro row until this one. AGENTS.md:57 carries the lane rule; runs/tasks.jsonl t12 is check_lane_respected, which detects occupancy after the fact.
incidents.root_cause: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is not additive: an assignment in a child replaces the parent's restriction instead of indexing into it, so any physical index escapes the lane the caller set.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: eval/_devs.sh is the one shard-to-card map; six scripts source it; harness check device_set_honoured walks every .sh for the class; _selftest_devs_map asserts the runtime mapping.
incidents.differently: Fix a class with a check, not five hand-edits. 2f97e4a edited three scripts by hand and both survivals below came out of that.

incidents.what: 2f97e4a's own fix still spilled. ${_DEVS[$i]:-$i} falls back to a physical index whenever the shard count exceeds the caller's card count, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 with eval_hard.sh's default N=6 maps shard 0 to card 7 and shards 1-5 to physical 1-5, five training-block cards.
incidents.caused_or_missed: missed by everyone for nine hours; found tonight while writing the check
incidents.evidence: reproduced against the pre-fix helper: _DEVS = 7 1 2 3 4 5. scripts/harness.py _selftest_devs_map asserts CVD=7 N=6 refuses; the old idiom fails that assert with exactly that array.
incidents.root_cause: The fallback was written for the unset-caller case and fires for the too-few-cards case as well. Two situations reach one branch and only one of them is safe.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: _devs.sh refuses a shard with no card to land on and names the count. An unset caller still gets the physical first N.
incidents.differently: A default that covers two situations needs them separated before the default is written.

incidents.what: eval_all.sh kept two bare CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 assignments for nine hours after 2f97e4a fixed its three callees. It is the top-level driver, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 eval/eval_all.sh still put the MC suite and the FoNE probe on physical GPU 0.
incidents.caused_or_missed: missed; found tonight by the grep the check is built on
incidents.evidence: eval/eval_all.sh, both lines now source eval/_devs.sh. scripts/harness.py _broken_device_set_honoured reverts line 54 and the check FAILs on it.
incidents.root_cause: The fix was scoped to the three scripts named in the incident report rather than to the pattern, and the driver that calls them was not in that list.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed with the check above, which walks every .sh in the tree.
incidents.differently: After fixing an instance, grep the whole tree for the pattern before closing.

incidents.what: I read `step 130/419 loss 1.288 19s` as 19 seconds per step and told fb the v3 SFT would take 2.3 h. The field is seconds per 10 logged steps (sft_math.py:235 resets t0 each log line), so the real answer was ~9 min. v2 had printed the same 20-23s and finished 419 steps in 15 min.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused, caught by fb before anything was scheduled on the wrong number
incidents.evidence: sft_math.py:235 prints time.time()-t0 with t0 reset at :236, one log line per 10 steps; v2's 13:32 start and 13:47 checkpoint bound it at 15 min for 419 steps
incidents.root_cause: I turned a log field into a duration without reading what the field counts. The log line names neither the unit nor the interval, so nothing contradicted me.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: proposed, not written: the log line should carry its interval (`19s/10steps`), which is a one-line change in a file frozen until the stage-1 run passes step 1000. Queued.
incidents.differently: Before a log number becomes an estimate, read the line that prints it. This is the same class as the ratio errors in docs/standards/0830v1_gates.md:844: a bare number does not carry its denominator.

incidents.what: score_matrix's degeneration metric truncates each generation to gen[-300:] and the comment justified it as 'the eval scripts store gen[-300:]'. Three of the five scorers have stored the full text since 89e7f9d; code_500 preds run to 1020 characters. The metric was discarding data already on disk and citing the disk as the reason.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused; I wrote the CJK half of that block tonight and carried the stale claim forward
incidents.evidence: eval/score_matrix.py DEGEN_CONFIG. Measured on p324 preds: whitespace code_500 58.2% tail vs 58.8% full, math_500 2.4%/2.4%, code_500_v2 81.4%/81.4%, every CJK field unchanged. Two scorers were still truncating: eval/code_fewshot.py:163 and eval/l1_fewshot.py:114, which 89e7f9d missed.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: both remaining scorers now store the full generation; the comment states the real reason and carries the measured cost; facts/base_eval.json#be.degeneration_rate no longer cites the stale code_zh.py:128. The window itself stays at 300 chars because widening it changes recorded numbers, which is fb's call. The 6.6% and 25.4% base-code figures rest on tail-only files and need a rerun to become re-derivable.
incidents.differently: A comment asserting a fact about another file is a claim to verify, not context to inherit.

class_removed: landed: physical-index device assignments. eval/_devs.sh is the single shard-to-card map, six scripts source it, harness check device_set_honoured greps every .sh for the class, and _selftest_devs_map proves the runtime mapping refuses the incident command (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 with N=6). The pre-fix idiom fails that assert, so the check has its failing case.

The edits are 029c43a at 19:48:58; the launch is d86bfc2 at 20:42:50, 54 minutes later, and the train.py blob has not changed since 19:48. Nothing was edited during the gate. The gap is still real and worth naming: nothing in the repo would have stopped it. pre-commit reads no running-run state, check_pod_drift SKIPs on a dev checkout, and the freeze lives in fb's order and a sentence in this file.
